text:
incident-bot: PAGE -> PagerDuty INC-2048: alert_high_error_rate firing x45 in 5m (service: inference-api, severity: P2). Escalating to oncall. https://pd.example/INC-2048

elaine: I'm oncall, looking. quick summary: lots of near-identical alerts from multiple pods in us-west1 — error 503 spikes on /generate. Customers affected: ~12 sessions, not a total outage.

jamal: thanks @elaine. can you confirm whether this is real errors or noisy retries? any request fingerprint commonality?

elaine: checking logs now. appears same upstream host failing (10.20.5.x) across 8 pods, so likely a backend dependency flapping. grouping key in alert is currently `instance` which is per-pod — causing PD dedupe to miss.

kiran: ugh. we saw this pattern last month. quick mitigation: 1) temporary rate-limit the PD rule (squelch duplicates for 2m) 2) change alertmanager grouping to use `fingerprint` label not `instance` and set `group_interval` to reduce churn 3) dashboard with aggregated traces for the calling upstream.

marta: I can push the alertmanager change now (small risk). propose this patch in alertmanager config:

```yaml
route:
  group_by: ['fingerprint', 'alertname']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 2m
  repeat_interval: 4h

# optional rate limiting in receiver config (via webhook throttling)
```

elaine: can we also add a quick PD dedupe rule? PagerDuty has dedup by `fingerprint` if we send that as `dedup_key` in our PD webhook. Might be faster than changing alertmanager routing.

jamal: agree — do both. I'll update the PD integration to include `fingerprint` in dedup_key and add a temporary suppression: allow 1 notify per fingerprint per 90s. That should stop the flood.

oncall-rotation-bot: Elaine hands off to Jamal at 11:30 PT.

elaine: filed a follow-up ticket infra-3456 to track the root cause with dependency owners. Noted customer impact and added to the incident doc.

marta: pushed alertmanager route change (staged) to canary replicas. Rolling out to all after 5m observation.

kiran: quick dashboard link for triage: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panelId=503&orgId=1 — added an aggregated series for /generate 5xx rate and upstream host histogram.

jamal: PD integration updated (dedup_key=fingerprint). Also added a short-rate-limit on our webhook receiver (max 3 events/2m per fingerprint). Will monitor.

elaine: after changes, alert volume dropped 92% in 6m. PagerDuty noise stopped. real errors reduced to single aggregated alert (tracking as INC-2048).

marta: next steps:
- create a long-term rule to group by fingerprint and service (not instance)
- add a playbook entry for dependency flapping (who to page and circuit-break)
- add a Grafana alert for the upstream host failure rate (lower severity)
- schedule a 1hr postmortem to decide on thresholds and retention

jamal: i'll own the PD side cleanup and runbook update. will open PRs for alertmanager and PD integration.

elaine: customer impact note added to incident doc: ~12 sessions affected, no data loss, temporary latency/errors for select tenants. Notifying account managers for the affected customers.

kiran: small suggestion for tuning: instead of huge repeat_interval, consider small `group_interval` + `receiver`-level dedupe so oncall still sees first real alert quickly but not the flood.

marta: agreed. i'll tune group_interval to 30s and group_interval for duplicate suppression to 2m; keep repeat_interval long. PR up: https://git.example/alertmgr/+/234.

jamal: closing loop — will leave a comment in the PR to coordinate with runbook changes. Thanks everyone. :+1:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE -> INC-2048 marked mitigated at 1769991347 by jamal. Postmortem scheduled.
